(Search snippet content — outlets' own reporting language. Replaces an earlier cache
file sourced to ofgem.gov.uk, which is NOT on the SOURCES.md approved-domain list.)

CNBC headline: "UK household energy bills to jump 13% amid Iran war energy shock"
Bloomberg headline: "UK Energy Price Cap Jumps 13% as Iran War Lifts Gas and Power Costs"
ITV News headline: "Energy bills to rise more than £200 a year as Iran war impacts UK households"

FACTS (cross-referenced across CNBC, ITV News and Bloomberg):
- The energy price cap rose 13% from 1 July 2026.
- Typical household gas and electricity bill: £1,641 a year previously; £1,862 from
  July — the highest level since early 2024.
- Gas bills up 24%; electricity bills up 5%.
- Driver: energy costs rose after Iran responded to US and Israeli attacks by blocking
  the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil and gas is carried.
- Roughly 40% of energy accounts across Britain are on fixed-term contracts and are
  shielded from the July rise.
